customer_name: VinuesaLab at the University of Michigan
business_problem: VinuesaLab needed high-fidelity, city-scale urban airflow simulation for planning and resilience work, but traditional CFD workflows were too slow, too resource intensive, and largely constrained to 2D approximations.
solution_summary: VinuesaLab built Diff-SPORT as an AI-driven urban-flow framework on NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo so the team could move from slow, 2D turbulence studies to scalable 3D reconstruction and real-time environmental emulation. The system combines generative models, physics-informed machine learning, and computational fluid-dynamics knowledge to reconstruct wind behavior, pollutant hotspots, and temperature changes across complex city layouts. RTX GPU acceleration speeds local training and experimentation, while an NVIDIA Academic Grant supplied A100 Tensor Core GPUs and 16,000 compute hours for larger runs and multi-node scaling. Because PhysicsNeMo supports distributed execution, the team can train on larger domains, integrate real city layouts, and reuse the same framework for collaborations in Europe and the United States instead of rebuilding separate simulation stacks for each deployment.

solution_components.name: Diff-SPORT
solution_components.role: Implements the generative urban-flow simulation framework researchers use to reconstruct and emulate turbulent city environments.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo
solution_components.role: Provides the physics-informed machine-learning framework that underpins training and scaling of the simulation models.

solution_components.name: RTX GPUs
solution_components.role: Accelerate local model training and experimentation for rapid iteration on urban-flow workloads.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs
solution_components.role: Provide larger-scale training capacity for high-resolution, multi-node research runs.

data_flow: Urban geometry, CFD context, and sensor observations are fed into Diff-SPORT on top of PhysicsNeMo, where GPU-accelerated training learns 3D flow reconstructions and real-time emulators. The resulting models generate wind, pollution, and temperature predictions that planners can visualize and test across full metropolitan layouts.
integration_points: Real city-layout collaborations in Europe and the US
business_outcome: VinuesaLab achieved 10x faster training, progressed from 2D analysis to interactive 3D urban-flow simulations, and built a real-time emulator that supports data-driven planning for wind, pollution, and urban-heat resilience studies.
architecture_clues: PhysicsNeMo supports seamless multi-node runs for larger metropolitan models
The project used eight A100 GPUs granted through NVIDIA's academic program
The team's work has been integrated back into the PhysicsNeMo repository
The framework is being extended to real city layouts in Barcelona and Southampton

Developed a real-time emulator capable of visualizing wind patterns, pollutant hotspots, and temperature changes.
